latest_apis.rationale: No UI framework is involved, so this comes down to the Vite/TS toolchain and DOM platform: both are on the exact current stable major, and the code uses current DOM/JS APIs throughout. No legacy patterns anywhere.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:133-140 — fetch + in-memory promise cache, no hand-rolled HTTP
app/src/pages/home.ts:14-38 — URLSearchParams for filter state, native <select>/<input type=search> with visible labels
app/src/components.ts:66 — loading="lazy" and decoding="async" on sprite images
app/src/main.ts:70-77 — navigation as a delegated document click listener over real <a href> links, so it degrades without JS

platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first almost everywhere; the one notable miss is using counters instead of AbortController to cancel stale requests, and the flat CSS misses modern nesting.

evidence: app/package.json:8-13 — zero runtime dependencies; devDependencies are only typescript and vite
app/src/dom.ts:8-29 — a ~20-line typed element helper instead of a rendering library

dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: nothing ships to the browser except the app's own code, and the two dev dependencies are both the latest stable majors.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:24-115 — all PokeAPI resources modeled as interfaces at the boundary; pages only consume typed data
app/src/api.ts:130-145 — every HTTP call goes through get/getResource, so a new API version would touch one module
app/src/url-state.ts:1-20 — URL mutation centralized in one tiny module
app/tsconfig.json:11-14 — strict, isolatedModules, noUnusedLocals
app/src/main.ts:20-27 vs app/server.mjs:36-45 — route patterns duplicated between client router and server 404 logic; adding a route means editing both, with no shared source of truth
app/server.mjs:30 vs app/src/api.ts:9 — the window.__API_BASE_URL__ injection convention is implicitly coupled across server and client with no shared constant
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, types, config, and URL state are all behind single well-defined modules and no framework internals are relied on; the one real churn point is the route table duplicated between server and client, plus the duplicated API-base injection convention.

findings.issue: Route patterns are duplicated between the client router (app/src/main.ts:20-27) and the server's 404-status logic; adding or renaming a route requires editing both files, and they can silently drift.
findings.suggestion: Extract one shared route table (patterns + resource kinds) into a module the server imports at runtime (e.g. src/routes.ts consumed by server.mjs alongside dist), so both sides derive from a single source of truth.

findings.issue: Stale navigations are handled with token counters (navigation in main.ts, token in pages/pokemon.ts:124-131) instead of cancelling the underlying fetch; superseded requests still consume network/API load.
findings.suggestion: Thread an AbortController through render/loadPage and call controller.abort() when a new navigation starts, passing its signal to fetch in api.ts.

findings.issue: The window.__API_BASE_URL__ global-injection convention is coupled by string matching between server.mjs and src/api.ts:9 with no shared constant or documented contract.
findings.suggestion: Give the injection a single owner (e.g. a shared key name exported from one module, or a JSON script tag the client parses), so changing the bootstrap format can't break one side silently.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache holds settled responses indefinitely (no TTL/eviction), fine for this data snapshot but the cache key is the raw URL, so any API_BASE_URL change at runtime would not be picked up.
findings.suggestion: Document the cache's lifetime assumption or key the cache on API_BASE_URL so the assumption is explicit if requirements change.

summary: A deliberately lean, framework-free app on the exact current stable toolchain (Vite 8, TypeScript 7 native) with zero runtime dependencies and consistently current DOM/platform APIs. Data access, types, config, and URL state are each behind one well-defined module, so API or framework changes would touch few files. The main forward-looking weakness is the route table duplicated between client and server, which will drift as routes are added.
